gaps: Complete supplied four-page main only; any SI and all 28 cited full sources remain unreviewed. Reference 28 is a source note about later theory, not independently checked here.

The common injection/growth range is 80–150 °C for 5–10 min, producing a continuous 3–8 nm series. Exact temperatures, times and physical batches are not assigned to the named 3, approximately 7 and approximately 8 nm outcomes.
Lead acetate hydration and reagent purities are unspecified. TOPSe is a 1 M solution, but its preparation and solvent are not supplied. Do not copy another article’s stock formulation.
The precursor is loaded into a 50 mL syringe; this is equipment capacity, not a measured injected volume. Injection rate and final precursor volume are unreported.

Storage hexane amount/time, butanol isomer, precipitation solvent ratio/volumes and centrifugation settings are not reported. The wording says the procedure was repeated twice; no normalized total-cycle count is invented.

The source reports rock-salt structure with the bulk lattice constant, but supplies no numeric lattice parameter, coordinates, refinement or exact sample assignment for Figure 1. Its lead-oleate impurity peaks remain explicit.

Figure 3 curves have no individual numeric size labels beyond the 3–8 nm series. Figure 5 contains three optical samples without sizes or per-curve quantum yields; no guessed size/recipe mapping or digitization is applied.

Lifetime 250 ns in Figure 6 is explicitly the 3 nm sample. The three separate Figure 5 lifetimes and uncertainties remain source context unless their sample mapping is explicit; no shared physical batch is inferred from coincident values.

source_notes.label: Why use colloidal PbSe quantum dots
source_notes.summary: The authors motivate PbSe by its strong confinement and infrared transitions. They cite electron, hole and exciton Bohr radii of 23, 23 and 46 nm and describe a 3–8 nm colloidal size range. These are background/model scales, not particle-coordinate measurements. The source’s stated R/aB range is retained without recalculation or redefinition.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and reported confinement range

source_notes.label: Temperature controls a series, not a supplied exact sample schedule
source_notes.summary: The paper varies injection and growth temperature within 80–150 °C and holds growth for 5–10 min. Higher temperatures produce larger dots, but it does not provide an exact temperature/time for each displayed size. The resulting record preserves that relationship without assigning endpoint temperatures to particular specimens.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Synthesis and size-control paragraphs

source_notes.label: Single injection and purification
source_notes.summary: Lead acetate and oleic acid are heated in phenyl ether, cooled, mixed with the reported TOPSe stock, then injected into hot phenyl ether. The paper gives syringe capacity but no measured precursor volume. Repeated precipitation and centrifugation remove excess reagents; size-selective precipitation is stated to be unnecessary under favorable conditions, not mandatory as a separate unreported step.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Synthesis and analytical sample preparation

source_notes.label: Structural evidence includes residual precursor
source_notes.summary: XRD is assigned to rock-salt PbSe and explicitly shows trace lead-oleate precursor peaks. STEM shows a close-packed ensemble and an approximately 7 nm lattice-resolved particle. The authors interpret its Pb-column image as a single crystal without internal defects, but no batch-wide defect fraction, shape distribution or atomic coordinate refinement is supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–2 and structure discussion

source_notes.label: Optical transitions are not all uniquely assigned
source_notes.summary: The authors compare the approximately 8 nm absorption spectrum with Kang’s model. First and third transitions agree, while the second feature is not accounted for by the allowed-transition calculation. Parity-forbidden transitions and band anisotropy are discussed as alternatives; the article favors the former but states that no decisive assignment is made. Model arrows and bars are not additional measured materials.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and transition interpretation; references 15 and 22

source_notes.label: High quantum yield does not prove a measured surface structure
source_notes.summary: The main reports room-temperature quantum yields of 12–81% without an inorganic semiconductor shell. Variation in surface reconstruction at reaction termination is suggested as an explanation, with comparison to earlier CdSe work. Actual surface reconstruction, ligand coverage and a per-size QY table are not measured.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and quantum-yield discussion; reference 27

source_notes.label: Long-lived emission and the later theoretical note
source_notes.summary: The 3 nm decay shown in Figure 6 has a 250 ns fitted time constant. The authors estimate an unscreened lowest-exciton transition-dipole radiative lifetime on the order of nanoseconds. They estimate that dielectric screening could increase it by as much as two orders of magnitude if bulk PbSe dielectric constants are assumed, while explicitly questioning whether bulk parameters apply to these nanocrystals. These are theoretical estimates, not additional measured lifetimes. Reference 28 adds a note that later calculations account for approximately 0.1 µs decay times; that cited full paper is not reviewed in this contribution, so the note remains source-attributed rather than independently confirmed.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 6, decay discussion and reference 28

source_notes.label: Stokes shifts and application outlook remain qualified
source_notes.summary: Ensemble Stokes shifts of 40–90 meV are reported, but excitation well above the lowest exciton prevents direct identification with an intrinsic single-particle spectrum. Vibronic/non-Franck–Condon effects are proposed. Optoelectronics and fluorescence microscopy are motivations; no device performance or biological test is reported here.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1, 3–4, Abstract, Stokes-shift discussion and outlook; reference 23

source_notes.label: Optical series with unresolved size assignment
source_notes.summary: Quantum yields 12–81%, Stokes shifts 40–90 meV and the three lifetime values 250±10,330±10 and 360±60 ns remain source context. Only the Figure 6 3 nm 250 ns fit is an explicitly sized lifetime. The curves are not invented additional recipes.
source_locators: Main PDF pp.3–4, Figures 3–6 and discussion
